subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps — Trustwell Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@trustwell.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps — Trustwell Health

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap so we have the same next steps and assumptions: 

Pain points you called out:
- Latency spikes for peak scheduling queries (particularly M-F 8am-10am PT) causing timeouts in your appointment booking flow.
- Data isolation requirements for PHI; must be behind a dedicated environment with customer-managed keys.
- Predictable unit economics — current cost variability from bursty workloads makes forecasting hard.

Goals we discussed:
- Move to a Dedicated capacity plan (reserved GPU pool) to guarantee throughput and isolation.
- Meet 99.9% uptime SLA with 95th percentile token latency under 150ms for the typical 512-token responses.
- Autoscaling to handle 3x baseline for planned campaign spikes with burst capacity for unforeseen events.

Proposed technical plan (high level):
1) Reserved capacity: start with 4 A100-equivalent GPUs (quantized 4-bit profile) — expected baseline throughput ~400 requests/min for your current model mix.
2) Isolation: Private VPC peering + KMS integration (you’ll manage CMK). We’ll provide SOC2 artifacts and an architecture diagram.
3) Scaling: autoscale policy to add 2 GPUs on sustained 2x load, burst pool of 2 additional GPUs for short spikes. Warm KV cache and prefix caching for recurring queries.
4) SLA/monitoring: Redwood Console dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, and an on-call escalation list for < 10-minute responses on SEV1 incidents.

Attachments included: Trustwell_Sizing_Estimate.xlsx (cost & sizing), SOC2-summary.pdf (controls overview).

Next steps / asks from Trustwell:
- Confirm commitment to start date window (we proposed week of Aug 23).
- Confirm CMK/provider for KMS and any networking constraints (IP allowlist or strict egress rules).
- Confirm the expected Q3 campaign weeks that will require burst capacity.

Internal next steps (copied): Dev — please prepare an initial commercial outline (term, price for reserved capacity + burst) and a draft MSA redline plan. Rishi — can you prepare the SOC2 evidence pack and network architecture diagram we can hand to Alyssa?

Alyssa, happy to hop back on a call to walk through the sizing sheet if helpful — propose 30 minutes Wed or Thu morning PT.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Dedicated Solutions
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-2198

--
Attachment stubs:
- Trustwell_Sizing_Estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet, 48KB)
- SOC2-summary.pdf (pdf, 120KB)

From: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@trustwell.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Garcia <t.garcia@trustwell.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps — Trustwell Health

Thanks Marissa — this is perfect and captures our discussion. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The peak latency issue is most visible between 8:00–10:30 PT weekdays; during those windows we need sub-200ms 95th percentile for the booking flow. If we can get 150ms at 95th that would be excellent.
- For KMS, we use Azure Key Vault with a customer-managed HSM-backed key — happy to share the tenant and key ID.
- Campaign spikes: we have scheduled outreach weeks Aug 30–Sep 3 and Sep 20–Sep 24; those are the highest risk windows.

We can commit to the week of Aug 23 for onboarding provided we have the SOC2 evidence and architecture diagram by Aug 16. Also, procurement will need a SOW + estimated monthly cost to start the internal purchase request.

For the call to review the sizing sheet, Thu 3 Aug 10:30am PT works for me — booking the invite now.

Best,
Alyssa
Head of Product Engineering
Trustwell Health
alyssa.turner@trustwell.com | (206) 555-0143

Thanks for the recap, Marissa. Quick notes for commercial: 
- Initial reserved commit: 4 GPUs monthly, with option to add 2 GPUs for burst at pre-agreed hourly rate.
- We should suggest a 12-month term with a 3-month ramp credit for onboarding (50% credit on first-month usage) to reduce procurement friction.
- MSA: expect basic redlines around indemnity and data handling; I'll pull a standard enterprise addendum for VPC/KMS.

I'll draft the commercial outline and share by EOD tomorrow. Rishi: if you can have the SOC2 pack and network diagram by Mon 8/16 that aligns with Alyssa's ask.
